skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render MP4 videos from React and Remotion TSX through the inference.sh CLI. It supports Remotion APIs, props, resolution, frame rate, duration, and codec settings.
skill.summary: Turn React and Remotion components into rendered MP4 videos through inference.sh.
skill.author: inference-shell

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks in documentation, code fences, or examples and are false positives for Ruby shell execution. The substantive risks are intentional remote rendering through inference.sh and missing guardrails for large render jobs. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Third-party code submission is not clearly disclosed before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Before running infsh, tell users that TSX code, props, and asset references are sent to inference.sh.

remediation.issue: Render size and duration limits are not documented.
remediation.suggestion: Document safe maximums for width, height, fps, and duration before invoking the renderer.

remediation.issue: Installation examples include npx commands outside the allowed tool scope.
remediation.suggestion: Keep install commands as manual setup steps and do not let the skill execute npx automatically.

static_findings.snippet: > Requires inference.sh CLI (`infsh`). Get installation instructions: `npx skills add inference-sh/s
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

semantic_findings.title: Remote Rendering Sends User Code to inference.sh
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash(infsh *) and examples run infsh/remotion-render with TSX in the code field. This sends user code and props to a third-party rendering service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools front matter and run examples explicitly show infsh remote app execution with TSX input. The risk is data disclosure to the service, not local command injection.

semantic_findings.title: Render Parameters Lack Cost Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The input schema exposes width, height, fps, and duration without documented upper bounds. Large values can create expensive or long-running remote render jobs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parameters are documented, but the skill file does not describe limits. The backend may enforce limits, so this is a guardrail issue rather than confirmed abuse.

content.value_statement: Programmatic video rendering can be slow to set up for React motion projects. This skill runs Remotion components through inference.sh and returns an MP4.
actual_capabilities: Runs infsh app run infsh/remotion-render with TSX component input.
Supports Remotion imports such as useCurrentFrame, spring, interpolate, AbsoluteFill, Sequence, Audio, Video, and Img.
Configures width, height, fps, duration, and codec.
Shows CLI and Python SDK workflows, including streaming progress.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated session.
Sends component code and props to inference.sh for rendering.
Only documented imports are Remotion and React.
The skill file does not state maximum render size or duration.

use_cases.title: Prototype Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Create quick Remotion animations as MP4 files without setting up a local render pipeline.

use_cases.title: Generate Product Videos
use_cases.description: Render branded launch clips or feature walkthrough animations from reusable React components.

use_cases.title: Automate Data Videos
use_cases.description: Use props to render charts, counters, or progress visuals from structured inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Intro
prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-render to create a three-second MP4 with centered title text, 1080p, 30 fps, and a fade-in animation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Social Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a square five-second Remotion video with a headline, subtitle, animated counter, and brand colors I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Use Props for Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Remotion component that accepts title, subtitle, and percentage props, then render two variants as MP4 outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Sequenced Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 10-second Remotion video with three timed sequences, spring transitions, asset placeholders, and streaming progress updates.

output_examples.input: Request: Render a three-second fade-in title animation at 1920 by 1080.
output_examples.output: An MP4 link is returned after the remote render completes.

output_examples.input: Request: Create a square animated progress counter with custom colors.
output: The component is rendered at 1080 by 1080.
The response includes the final video URL.

output_examples.input: Request: Stream progress for a longer Remotion render.
output_examples.output: Progress updates are shown during rendering, followed by the video output URL.

best_practices: Confirm before sending private code, props, or asset URLs to inference.sh.
Keep duration, resolution, and frame rate within the smallest acceptable values.
Use props for content variants instead of rewriting the full component.
anti_patterns: Do not embed secrets, tokens, or private customer data in TSX or props.
Do not request very large renders without confirming limits and cost.
Do not install related skills or packages unless the user approves setup changes.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion component code into MP4 video through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires the infsh CLI and an authenticated inference.sh session.

faq.question: Can it use Remotion animations?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, Sequence, and other Remotion APIs.

faq.question: Can I pass dynamic content?
faq.answer: Yes. The input schema supports props for titles, subtitles, values, and other component data.

faq.question: Where is the code rendered?
faq.answer: The examples run infsh/remotion-render, so code and props are sent to inference.sh.

faq.question: What should I avoid sending?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, private customer data, unreleased source code, and confidential asset URLs.
